Police dispersed demonstrators in Nanyuki, 120 miles from Nairobi, amid rising anger at US plans

Kenyan police have shot dead a man during a protest against a proposed Ebola quarantine facility for US citizens.

Patrick Wahome, who has organised protests in Nanyuki against the centre, told Reuters on Tuesday the man died from a gunshot wound to the head. Reporters from the agency saw his body lying motionless in a police van with a large head wound.

Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira faces fraud charges after allegedly persuading family to take her into their home

A 38-year-old woman has been arrested in Brazil accused of pretending to be a 12-year-old girl to deceive a couple who took her into their home for more than a year.

Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira was charged in the southern state of Santa Catarina with fraud and false identity offences.

guardian.description:
Twenty people were killed and 120 injured in the attack at the Erawan Shrine, a popular tourist destination

A Thai court has handed out death sentences to two Uyghur men from the north-western Chinese region of Xinjiang for a 2015 bombing in the centre of Bangkok that killed 20 people.

Critically endangered Tapanuli orangutan population falls after heavy rain and landslides, fuelled by climate crisis, in North Sumatra

guardian.description:
Renewed outrage at White House’s use manga and anime imagery after US president is depicted as ninja Naruto

Japanese anime and manga fans are urging Donald Trump to stop using their favourite characters in his social media posts.

About 20,000 people have signed a petition on Change.org entitled Protect Japanese Manga, protesting against the official White House X account posting videos featuring unauthorised use of imagery from the popular Dragon Ball, Yu-Gi-Oh! and Naruto series.

guardian.description:
People told not to enter damaged buildings for fear of aftershocks from magnitude-7.8 quake

At least 37 people have died and hundreds have been injured after a magnitude-7.8 earthquake shook part of the southern Philippines early on Monday, collapsing buildings and triggering tsunami alerts.

guardian.description:
Kim Jong-un welcomes Chinese leader on visit to renew relations strained amid Pyongyang’s closeness with Russia

Xi Jinping has arrived in North Korea for a two-day trip, his first in nearly seven years, as China’s leader looks to revitalise ties with his junior ally.

Footage published by China’s Xinhua state news agency showed an Air China plane carrying Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, touching down at Pyongyang’s Sunan international airport.

rfi.title: How Cabo Delgado's riches became fuel for the Islamist insurgency in Mozambique
rfi.description: For almost a decade, an Islamist group has terrorised Mozambique's northern province of Cabo Delgado. Despite vast reserves of rubies, timber and natural gas, the region remains the country's poorest. This first instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories to which RFI contributed – examines how exploitation of the region's wealth, corruption and alleged abuses by security forces helped fuel the insurgency.

rfi.title: Mexico and South Africa kick off first 48-team football World Cup
rfi.description: Mexico and South Africa will launch the first 48-team football World Cup on Thursday with a game at the Estadio Azteca in Mexico City.

rfi.title: Killing of gay man to be investigated as homophobic crime following protests
rfi.description: Police investigating the murder of a young gay man in the eastern French city of Metz have said the case will now be treated as a homophobic crime, after protestations from rights groups and politicians.

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

rfi.title: RFI denounces violation of press freedom after French reporter barred by Israel
rfi.description: RFI has condemned Israel's decision to refuse entry to journalist Alice Froussard, describing the move as "an obstacle to press freedom". Froussard, who reports on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict for French media, including RFI, was turned away on arrival at Tel Aviv airport and sent back without explanation.

rfi.title: Climate report shows 1.5C limit on global warming will be breached by 2030
rfi.description: Human-induced global warming is on track to reach 1.5C around 2030, a group of leading scientists said on Thursday.

rfi.title: Fifa grants World Cup accreditation to jailed French journalist Christophe Gleizes
rfi.description: In a move hailed by press freedom campaigners as an important gesture of solidarity, Fifa has issued World Cup accreditation to French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who has been detained in Algeria for more than a year.

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel charged with rape and sexual assault
rfi.description: French singer and actor Patrick Bruel has been charged with rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and sexual harassment, prosecutors said on Wednesday, in a case that now involves accusations by more than 20 women.

rfi.title: Amnesty accuses Israel of ‘ethnic cleansing’ of West Bank Bedouin communities
rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused Israel of carrying out what it described as a state-led campaign of “ethnic cleansing” against Bedouin and herding communities in the occupied West Bank, saying the measures were intended to accelerate the annexation of Palestinian territory.

rfi.title: Europe faces growing threat from synthetic opioids and new drugs, report warns
rfi.description: Highly potent synthetic opioids are spreading through Europe's fast-changing drug market, linked to hundreds of deaths as traffickers shift to smaller ports and new smuggling methods, the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA) has warned.

rfi.title: European heatwave drives world's second-hottest May on record
rfi.description: The world experienced its second-hottest May on record in 2026 as an unusually early and intense heatwave swept across Europe, setting new temperature records across the continent, the European Union's Copernicus Climate Change Service said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Pope Leo to celebrate mass at Barcelona's unfinished Sagrada Familia
rfi.description: Pope Leo XIV will celebrate mass at Barcelona's Sagrada Família on Wednesday and bless its final tower, marking the completion of Antoni Gaudí's masterpiece and making it the tallest church in the world. The pontiff arrived in Spain at the weekend for a week-long visit focused on immigration and politics.

rfi.title: Kenyan protester killed at demonstration against US Ebola facility
rfi.description: Kenyan police shot dead a protester on Tuesday as hundreds demonstrated against a government-backed quarantine centre for Americans exposed to Ebola, with anger mounting over Nairobi's determination to press ahead with the facility.

rfi.title: Belfast unrest erupts after stabbing linked to Sudanese refugee
rfi.description: Belfast anti-immigration protesters set vehicles and buildings on fire on Tuesday night, a day after a knife attack allegedly carried out by a Sudanese refugee seriously injured a man and was captured in a graphic video that spread widely online.

rfi.title: Africa's finest: Ghana to seek World Cup redemption under new coach Queiroz
rfi.description: Ghana enter the first 48-team World Cup ranked 14th among African sides in the Fifa standings. In the final instalment of a nine-part series on African squads at the 2026 tournament, hosted across the United States, Mexico and Canada, RFI looks at a nation making its fifth World Cup appearance.

rfi.title: French PM announces measures to combat child abuse amid Lyhanna protests
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Tuesday presented initial measures to better protect children, following a meeting with key ministers, in a bid to quell public anger sweeping the country over the death of 11-year-old Lyhanna.

rfi.title: Oxfam warns Europe’s corporate giants are fuelling inequality
rfi.description: Europe’s biggest companies are paying more than two-thirds of their profits to shareholders on average, diverting money that could otherwise support investment, climate action and workers’ wages, according to Oxfam.

rfi.title: France moves closer to ocean goals with three new marine protection zones
rfi.description: The French government has announced three new marine protected areas, bringing it a step closer to goals established at the 2025 United Nations Ocean Summit. These "strong protection" zones are situated in mainland France, in the French West Indies and the French Southern and Antarctic Lands.

euronews.title: Lagarde defends ECB interest rate hike as ‘robust across three scenarios’
euronews.description: Critics worry the decision to keep rates high could hit productivity and keep inflation from returning to target levels until 2027.

euronews.title: IMF warns against further relaxation of euro area fiscal rules
euronews.description: The IMF has urged euro area countries to tighten their fiscal policies rather than relaxing them further in response to the energy crisis, with an extra adjustment effort required from high-debt nations.

euronews.title: No option but to talk to Taliban about migrant returns, EU's migration commissoner says
euronews.description: EU countries received about a million asylum applications filed by Afghans between 2013-2024, according to the bloc's data agency.

euronews.title: Pope Leo XIV casts wreath into sea in memory of migrants lost on Atlantic route
euronews.description: Pope Leo XIV threw a floral wreath into the waters off Spain's Canary Islands to honour migrants who died attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing. The pontiff also condemned indifference to the plight of migrants during his visit.

euronews.title: Kallas defends EU foreign service before staff as debate over its future intensifies
euronews.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas has backed her own diplomatic service as European capitals, led by Paris, eye a possible EEAS overhaul, ranging from stripping the High Representative's powers to expanding them.

euronews.title: Three dead after car ploughs into school cycling group in the Netherlands
euronews.description: The accident happened near the village of Vogelwaarde, close to the Belgian border, and the ages of the children involved are not currently known.

euronews.title: Portugal triggers EU budget safeguard clause over energy crisis
euronews.description: The EU safeguard clause allows member states to cover energy-related costs in response to the crisis, just as they did in the field of defence.

euronews.title: Poverty shapes children's brains more than parenting or IQ, study says
euronews.description: A family’s financial status plays a major role in children’s brain development, according to a new study.

euronews.title: Senior MEP fears Airbus-Boeing dispute could reignite EU-US tensions
euronews.description: German MEP Bernd Lange fears the end of a crucial corporate truce could give the US grounds to breach the Turnberry agreement, which the European Parliament is expected to adopt next week.

euronews.title: Cyprus proposes €32.8bn cut to next EU budget as compromise between rival camps
euronews.description: Cyprus proposes a 2% cut — worth €32.8bn — to the EU's draft €2 trillion budget for 2028–2034, in a bid to bridge the gap between "frugals" and cohesion-minded member states. The figures, now on the table for the first time, will serve as the starting point for the sensitive negotiations ahead.

euronews.title: These underrated natural wonders are the world’s best-kept secrets
euronews.description: From Alaska’s glaciers to a remote Scottish island famed for its puffins and dramatic sea cave, new research based on 54,000 reviews reveals the hidden natural wonders travellers say deserve far more attention – and the famous sites that fail to live up to the hype.

euronews.title: First group of Nigerians returns home after anti-immigration protests in South Africa
euronews.description: Authorities in South Africa said the returnees were found to be in the country illegally, contradicting Nigerian officials who they were fleeing xenophobic attacks.

euronews.title: Rising housing costs are pushing more Europeans into homelessness, report says
euronews.description: The increased cost of living is weighing on Europeans' rights, an EU agency said in a report published Thursday, citing rising housing costs that are making people homeless.

euronews.title: ILA Berlin: Fighter jets still fly but drones dominate the conversation
euronews.description: While flight displays and military hardware continue to draw the crowds, drones, autonomous systems and a new generation of defence companies are increasingly shaping the conversation at ILA Berlin.

euronews.title: Meloni tells Brussels to scrap 'rebates' for some member states – or Italy will demand them too
euronews.description: The Italian Prime Minister has attacked the EU's disbursement to so-called frugal states and warned Brussels that Rome's patience with them is at an end.

euronews.title: German, French and UK envoys meet Lavrov's deputy in Moscow amid E3 peace push
euronews.description: Earlier this month, Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Volodymyr Zelenskyy's offer for a face-to-face meeting to end the fighting.

euronews.title: Somali referee denied entry to the US set to officiate UEFA Super Cup final
euronews.description: The Super Cup final sees the winners of the Champions League face off against the holders of the Europa League. It is set to take place on 12 August at Stadion Salzburg in Austria.

lemonde.title: Affaire Lyhanna : Jérôme Barella avait été signalé à la police française par un organisme antipédocriminalité américain
lemonde.description: Une activité en ligne suspecte de l’homme soupçonné d’avoir tué Lyhanna a été relevée par le NCMEC, un organisme de référence qui agrège les alertes collectées par les fournisseurs d’accès à Internet, les géants du Web et les réseaux sociaux.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, Mexique - Afrique du Sud : la cérémonie d’ouverture de la Coupe du monde va débuter au stade Azteca de Mexico
lemonde.description: Pays organisateur avec les Etats-Unis et le Canada, le Mexique lance, jeudi, la Coupe du monde 2026 de football à Mexico. Il affronte l’Afrique du Sud, comme lors du match d’ouverture du Mondial 2010.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : face aux candidatures d’Edouard Philippe et de Gabriel Attal, le camp présidentiel à l’heure des doutes
lemonde.description: Aucun des deux anciens premiers ministres ne réussit, pour l’instant, à fédérer les élus du bloc central. Beaucoup redoutent un duel fratricide qui ferait disparaître l’espace créé par Emmanuel Macron.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : Donald Trump affirme qu’il va frapper l’Iran « très fort ce soir »
lemonde.description: « Les Etats-Unis frapperont l’Iran (dont la marine, l’armée de l’air, les radars, la défense antiaérienne et toutes les autres formes de défense, ainsi que la majeure partie des capacités offensives, ont disparu) TRÈS FORT ce soir », a écrit le président américain sur son réseau social, après de premières attaques dans la nuit de mercredi à jeudi.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : Sébastien Lecornu fixe une « ligne rouge » concernant le renouvellement du titre de séjour de Xenia Fedorova
lemonde.description: Interrogé sur la place croissante accordée à l’ancienne dirigeante de la chaîne d’Etat russe RT, Xenia Fedorova, dans les médias du milliardaire conservateur Vincent Bolloré, Sébastien Lecornu a estimé jeudi qu’il y avait « un combat politique à mener ».

lemonde.title: Immigration : les nouvelles règles européennes durcies en matière d’asile entrent en application
lemonde.description: Négocié pendant dix ans, un ensemble de textes durcit les règles applicables aux demandeurs d’asile à leur arrivée, accélère le traitement de leur situation et institue un fragile mécanisme de solidarité entre pays. Mais tous les Etats, dont la France, n’ont pas encore suffisamment adapté leur législation.

lemonde.title: Aux Canaries, le pape Léon XIV dénonce « l’indifférence » envers les migrants : « Nous ne pouvons pas nous accoutumer à compter les morts »
lemonde.description: Le chef de l’Eglise catholique achève, jeudi et vendredi, sa visite en Espagne dans l’archipel que s’efforcent d’atteindre des exilés venus du continent africain voisin. Dans le même registre que son prédécesseur, François, il a affirmé que leurs destins interrogent « ce qu’il reste de notre humanité ».

lemonde.title: Royaume-Uni : le ministre de la défense, John Healey, en désaccord avec Keir Starmer, démissionne
lemonde.description: Le ministre de la défense britannique a annoncé jeudi sa démission, exprimant son désaccord à propos d’un plan d’investissement à long terme dans la défense.

lemonde.title: La nationalisation d’ArcelorMittal de nouveau votée par l’Assemblée nationale
lemonde.description: Les députés ont voté, jeudi 11 juin, en deuxième lecture pour la nationalisation des activités françaises du numéro deux mondial de l’acier. Soutenue par l’ensemble des partis de gauche, la proposition de loi a été rejetée par le gouvernement et la droite. Le RN, embarrassé, s’est abstenu. Le texte doit être à nouveau examiné par le Sénat.

lemonde.title: Boualem Sansal : Gallimard dénonce les accusations portées par l’écrivain franco-algérien
lemonde.description: Dans « La Légende », sorti le 2 juin chez Grasset, l’auteur de 81 ans se montre particulièrement sévère avec les dirigeants de Gallimard, qu’il met en cause pour leurs positions pendant et après sa détention en Algérie.

lemonde.title: Israël refuse l’entrée sur son territoire à Alice Froussard, journaliste française
lemonde.description: La journaliste, qui couvre depuis plusieurs années le conflit israélo-palestinien pour Radio France et RFI, a été « expulsée et remise dans un avion pour la France », ont annoncé les autorités israéliennes.

lemonde.title: Aix-Marseille-Provence : la chambre régionale des comptes invite la Métropole à réduire sa dotation aux communes de 53 millions d’euros
lemonde.description: Chargés d’élaborer le budget 2026 de l’établissement public, les magistrats proposent également 65 millions d’euros d’économies de fonctionnement mais écartent l’hypothèse d’une hausse d’impôts.

lemonde.title: « Nouveaux OGM » : semenciers et sélectionneurs de semences s’inquiètent d’une possible brevetabilité des plantes
lemonde.description: La commission environnement du Parlement européen doit voter, lundi 15 juin, la dérégulation des plantes issues des nouvelles techniques génomiques, qui devraient être protégées par des brevets. Une évolution perçue comme une menace par le secteur de la production de semences, très dynamique en France.

lemonde.title: Cyberattaques : sept personnes interpellées, soupçonnées d’avoir volé plusieurs dizaines de millions de données sensibles
lemonde.description: Plus de 1 500 sociétés ou entités, dont l’Assemblée nationale, mais aussi des sites médicaux pourraient être victimes de ces hackeurs français.

lemonde.title: La mairie RN de Carcassonne refuse de prêter ses locaux pour le vote d’Algériens
lemonde.description: Le consulat d’Algérie avait sollicité la commune pour y installer des bureaux de vote destinés aux ressortissants algériens établis en France, appelés aux urnes pour les élections législatives du 2 juillet.

lemonde.title: El Niño, le phénomène climatique qui réchauffe les températures dans le Pacifique équatorial, a commencé
lemonde.description: L’Agence américaine d’observation océanique et atmosphérique estime à 63 % le risque d’un épisode très fort, avec des températures pouvant dépasser de 2 degrés les moyennes dans la région entre novembre et janvier.

lemonde.title: « Rebonds, une épopée de la danse électro », sur Arte.tv : retour sur un phénomène de culture urbaine aux multiples avatars
lemonde.description: En quatre épisodes étourdissants, Marianne Getti et Loïc Phil décryptent le mouvement apparu il y a deux décennies en France et qui connut un essor fulgurant sous l’étiquette « Tecktonik ».

france24fr.title: Trump dit "adorer" l’inflation, une "tentative désespérée de prouver qu’il contrôle la situation"
france24fr.description: Interrogé sur le taux de l’inflation aux États-Unis, qui a bondi de 4,2 % en un an, Donald Trump a salué mercredi des "chiffres supers", déclarant "adorer l’inflation", qu’il avait pourtant promis de faire "disparaitre" durant sa campagne.

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : un dysfonctionnement structurel de la justice ?
france24fr.description: La mort de Lyhanna a marqué une rupture de confiance des Français envers leurs institutions – notamment la justice, qui a échoué à protéger la jeune fille. Au-delà des responsabilités individuelles ou collectives, n’est-ce pas le système politique, en imposant ses lois ou ses visions successives, qui a éteint toute velléité pour les administrations de gagner en autonomie et de se corriger de l’intérieur ?

france24fr.title: Lutte contre les ingérences numériques : "La France est dans le top 3 européen"
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a réuni jeudi les formations politiques pour aborder la question des ingérences électorales. À l’approche de la présidentielle, les autorités françaises redoutent des tentatives de manipulation numérique venues de l’étranger, dont l'efficacité est décuplée par les progrès de l'intelligence artificielle. Entretien avec Benoît Grünemwald, expert en cybersécurité à Eset.

france24fr.title: Le pape en Espagne : hommage aux migrants morts en mer
france24fr.description: En visite aux Canaries, le Pape Léon XIV a rendu hommage aux migrants morts dans l’Atlantique en lançant un bouquet de fleurs à la mer. Il a aussi dénoncé l’indifférence de beaucoup face à leur sort.

france24fr.title: Ambiance surchauffée au Mondial... Et ce n'est pas une bonne nouvelle!
france24fr.description:
Plusieurs matchs de ce Mondial vont se dérouler sous une chaleur écrasante. Des conditions qui pourront être difficiles à supporter pour les joueurs et pour les spectateurs. Toutes les équipes ne sont d'ailleurs pas logées à la même enseigne et cela peut influencer les résultats.
 
Comment la chaleur affecte la santé et les performance des footballeurs? On vous explique tout.

france24fr.title: Cette vidéo de la destruction d’un hélicoptère américain par l’Iran a été générée par IA
france24fr.description: Une supposée vidéo de la destruction d’un hélicoptère d’attaque américain Apache par l’armée iranienne a récolté plusieurs millions de vues sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle a pourtant été créée par intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : le Pentagone placé en confinement pour une fausse alerte
france24fr.description: Une partie du Pentagone, siège du département de la Défense américaine, a été placée jeudi en confinement et évacuée. Les pompiers sont intervenus pour un potentiel "incident lié à des matières ‌dangereuses", qui était en réalité une fausse alerte, selon CNN.

france24fr.title: Pour le 80e anniversaire de Donald Trump, la Maison Blanche prépare… une arène de MMA XXL
france24fr.description: Pour son anniversaire dimanche prochain, mais aussi pour les 250 ans de l’indépendance des États-Unis, Donald Trump et la Maison Blanche préparent un événement grandiose : une arène de MMA XXL où six combats d’UFC auront lieu.

france24fr.title: Ce qu'il faut dans sa valise quand on est un journaliste qui couvre la Coupe du monde
france24fr.description: Des objets utiles, nécessaires, voire absolument indispensables. Voici ce que contient la valise d'un journaliste qui part couvrir la Coupe du monde de football !

france24fr.title: RD Congo : des bénévoles de la Croix-Rouge attaqués en plein enterrement des victimes d'Ebola
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, la Croix-Rouge a dénonce, dans un communiqué, une attaque contre des volontaires lors d’une opération d’inhumation au cœur de l’épicentre de l’épidémie d’Ebola. Ces attaques sont de plus en plus fréquentes. Récit d'Emily Boyle.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Lecornu présente ses réponses face aux ingérences étrangères
france24fr.description: Désireux de "protéger le débat démocratique", Sébastien Lecornu expose jeudi aux partis politiques et à la presse les moyens pour mieux lutter contre les ingérences étrangères aux élections, qui pourraient s'intensifier à l'approche de la présidentielle.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : démission du ministre britannique de la Défense, en désaccord avec Starmer
france24fr.description: Le ministre britannique de la Défense John Healey a annoncé jeudi sa démission, exprimant son désaccord avec le Premier ministre Keir Starmer à propos d'un plan d'investissement dans la défense qui doit être publié prochainement.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : le Mexique, berceau ancestral du jeu de balle
france24fr.description: Le coup d’envoi de la Coupe du monde est donné à 21h, heure de Paris. Le Mexique ouvre la compétition. Malgré les manifestations, la fan zone du Zócalo à Mexico restera ouverte, assure la présidente Claudia Sheinbaum. C’est la troisième fois que le pays accueille le Mondial, un record lié à une longue tradition du jeu de balle dans la région, vieille de près de 3 500 ans.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : Mexico prêt à donner le coup d'envoi d'un tournoi inédit et sous tension
france24fr.description: Le "futbol" s'apprête à reprendre ses droits avec le match d'ouverture du Mondial-2026 opposant le Mexique à l'Afrique du Sud jeudi à 13h00 locales, sur fond de tensions géopolitiques et de polémiques en séries.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : l’absence de l’Italie éloigne les supporters italiens
france24fr.description: L’absence de l’Italie au Mondial 2026 laisse un vide pour ses supporters. Privés de compétition, beaucoup d’entre eux se montrent moins concernés par le tournoi, qui perd ainsi une partie de son public traditionnel en Italie.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : quel rôle et quelle stratégie pour Donald Trump ?
france24fr.description: Après le Mexique jeudi et le Canada en début d'après-midi, la Coupe du monde débute vendredi soir aux Etats-Unis avec un match entre le Paraguay et la sélection américaine, en quête d'enthousiasme mais boudée par Donald Trump.Les précisions de Carole Gomez, chercheuse associée à l'IRIS, spécialiste en géopolitique du sport.

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : un révélateur des failles de la justice française ?
france24fr.description: Dans le sillage de l'affaire Lyhanna, policiers et gendarmes ont l'injonction de passer en revue, en lien avec les parquets, toutes les procédures pour des infractions sexuelles commises sur des mineurs: une tâche "impossible" à réaliser sur fond de crise de l'investigation dans la police.

france24fr.title: Mourad Farès, ex-recruteur de jihadistes pour la Syrie, déchu de sa nationalité française
france24fr.description: L'ancien recruteur de jihadistes Mourad Farès a été déchu jeudi de sa nationalité française, selon un décret paru au Journal officiel. undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

phys-org.title: Rare deep-sea goblin sharks filmed in natural habitat for first time
phys-org.description: The first published live observations of the rare goblin shark (Mitsukurina owstoni) in its natural deep-ocean habitat were reported in a new paper by a University of Hawai'i at Mānoa-led team of oceanographers. In the past, goblin sharks were filmed and reported alive only after being hooked on a fishing line and hauled to the surface, where divers could observe them and where they soon died. The new study, published in Journal of Fish Biology, documents two live observations of one of the

phys-org.title: AI doesn't just help us think, it thinks instead of us: What this means for the process of learning
phys-org.description: Deep in Book VII of Plato's Republic, Socrates describes prisoners chained inside a cave, mistaking shadows cast on a wall by firelight for reality itself. They name the shadows, debate them and develop expertise about them. The prisoners are completely, sincerely wrong, and they have no idea. The cave isn't a place of stupidity; it's a place of convincing, well-organized illusion.

phys-org.title: Amazon deforestation is falling, but progress is stalling
phys-org.description: In 2025, the area deforested in the country fell below 1 million hectares in a year for the first time since 2019. A total of 984,794 hectares of native vegetation were cleared during 2025, a reduction of 20.6% compared with 2024.

phys-org.title: Why animal calls sound alike in time: Most species share a common communication tempo
phys-org.description: From insects to great apes, by way of birds and fish, animals communicate through an extraordinary variety of sounds. While the pitch or timbre of their vocalizations matters, rhythm may play a more fundamental role. Scientists from the University of Geneva (UNIGE), the NCCR Evolving Language, the reConnect Institute and the Institut Pasteur analyzed more than 2,000 sound recordings produced by 98 animal species. phys-org.title: Ocean glow meets 3D printing with living gels that sense mechanical force
phys-org.description: The integration of biological organisms into synthetic structures offers a radical new pathway for developing intelligent, self-powered materials. Researchers have pioneered an innovative approach to biomanufacturing by using light-based 3D printing to engineer living material systems capable of localized environmental processing.

phys-org.title: Municipal governments are often slow to act, except when FIFA comes to town
phys-org.description: With the 2026 FIFA World Cup kicking off, millions of soccer fans around the world will be following the tournament taking place across 16 host cities in Canada, Mexico and the United States.

phys-org.title: Novel nanowire device offers rapid, noninvasive cancer detection
phys-org.description: A research team in Japan has developed an efficient, minimally invasive cancer detection device that uses high-performance zinc oxide nanowires to selectively capture extracellular vesicles (EVs) from bodily fluids.

phys-org.title: Earth's energy imbalance has doubled—here's why that matters
phys-org.description: Heat waves across Europe and South Asia have dominated the news recently. But these events are really a surface expression of more fundamental changes affecting our planet: Earth itself is accumulating heat faster than ever before.

phys-org.title: How a shape-shifting tiny rover inspired by Japanese toys autonomously explored the moon
phys-org.description: Moon missions come in all shapes and sizes, from car-sized rovers packed with scientific equipment to towering rocket payloads—and now, a small, shape-shifting machine that is about the size of the average palm.

phys-org.title: Life after death: From burned trees to bleached corals, how dead organisms live on as the building blocks of new life
phys-org.description: People's knee-jerk reaction to seeing death in nature is often not positive. The burn scar left by wildfire on a once-forested hillside, or a ghostly white coral reef, may evoke tragedy and despair. But in nature, most plants and animals are recycled into new life.

phys-org.title: Why shame is an evolution-based defense mechanism
phys-org.description: It is unpleasant, strange and often comes as a surprise: shame. But why do we feel it? An international study has shed new light on the emotion of shame, which has long been considered harmful. The conclusion: Shame is not merely an inconvenient feeling, but may fulfill an important function. As an evolution-based protective mechanism, it can help us protect our social reputation.

phys-org.title: Private space tourism is taking off—but laws on outer space are from another era
phys-org.description: Private commercial operators are launching more rockets into space, carrying more people and pursuing more ambitious missions than ever before.

phys-org.title: Massive Kamchatka earthquake has extended rupture that overlaps 1952 event, researchers find
phys-org.description: Researchers combining two methods to reconstruct the rupture evolution of the July 2025 magnitude 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake found the rupture from the megathrust event extended about 500 kilometers (311 miles) from its epicenter.

phys-org.title: Farmers are key to restoring native woodlands—here's what's holding them back
phys-org.description: Ireland's native woodland scheme, which was introduced by the government in 2001, is successfully bringing back biodiversity. But the country still struggles to meet its tree-planting targets. The reason? Policy doesn't always match the economic realities farmers face.

phys-org.title: 'Janus-faced' nanomaterials pave the way for selectively capturing radioactive pollutants
phys-org.description: A KAIST research team has succeeded, for the first time, in synthesizing the core raw material for fabricating asymmetric MXene, a so-called "Janus-faced" nanomaterial that can perform distinct functions because of differing atomic compositions on its two sides, paving the way for the development of multifunctional materials with applications such as removing radioactive pollutants and shielding electromagnetic waves.

phys-org.title: Firms with independent board members are more willing to challenge risky CEO pay structures, says new research
phys-org.description: The study, published in European Financial Management, focused on "inside debt," which includes pensions and deferred compensation awarded to chief executives. Unlike bonuses or shares, these payments can encourage CEOs to become more cautious because their personal wealth becomes more tied to the company's long-term financial health.

phys-org.title: How Hurricane Dorian changed disaster reporting
phys-org.description: When Hurricane Dorian slammed into the Bahamas on Sept. 1, 2019, its Category 5 winds devastated two islands over three days, destroyed infrastructure, left thousands missing or homeless, and caused more than 70 recorded deaths.

phys-org.title: Ancient clay figurine from Guatemala may bear the oldest written numbers in Mesoamerica
phys-org.description: A clay figurine, small enough to cradle in your hand, with 11 dots arranged in columns where its head should be, may depict the oldest known example of written numbers in Mesoamerica.

public-dom.description: In the Middle Ages, rumours spread across Europe of a strange hybrid creature, half-animal, half-plant, known as the Vegetable Lamb of Tartary. A hoax based on fern rhizomes? proj-syn.title: The Democrats Need a Story, Not More Lists
proj-syn.description: Whereas Donald Trump has offered voters a clear and compelling narrative, Democrats have provided only vague aspirations and long lists of policies. To win over voters—rather than scrounging protest votes—they must articulate a compelling economic vision, with wage-led growth as its foundation.

proj-syn.title: What if Europe Loses Access to Its Climate Data?
proj-syn.description: The European Green Deal runs on data, from corporate disclosures to climate-risk analyses and decarbonization pathways. But much of this data feeds platforms and tools developed outside the European Union, which could threaten the bloc’s climate agenda and even its foundational values.

proj-syn.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
proj-syn.description: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

proj-syn.title: Peak Oil Demand Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: Amid the disruptions caused by the US/Israeli-Iran war, countries have begun adapting to life with less oil. What started as a supply shock has become a demand story, forcing the energy sector to reconsider one of its most important assumptions: continued growth of global oil demand.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.
